question: Can a precomputed avatar support convincing arbitrary Russian speech on a Mac without live server GPU inference?
hypotheses: Mouth sprite retrieval is fast on CPU but has limited coarticulation and head motion
A compact neural mouth renderer over preprocessed video offers a better quality-resource tradeoff
baseline: Frozen current Pipecat project; isolated experiments only
inputs: Public synthetic/licensed demo avatar and local synthetic Russian audio; no personal face without consent
primary: Human judgement of mouth timing and transition artifacts, not a fabricated score
guardrails: CPU inference runtime versus audio duration
Do not confuse integrated graphics with CPU-only
No API expenditure beyond agreed cap
test_split: Same held-out Russian phrases across variants; no training or prompt tuning on final phrases
stop_rule: One retrieval baseline and one feasible lightweight implementation; stop setup paths needing absent authority or unresolved asset license
gpu: Read-only check found own StatefulSet scaled to zero; activation approval requested
